programme.desc: Research is revealing that sharks can be sociable and intelligent, but these breakthroughs come just as many sharks face extinction. Science may now be the only way to save them.

programme.title: Horizon
programme.desc: Volcanoes have long helped shape the Earth. This is a look at the work of an international team of volcanologists in Iceland as they draw fascinating parallels with the volcanoes on Earth and those elsewhere in the solar system.

programme.title: Concorde: A Supersonic Story
programme.desc: The life of the most glamorous plane ever built, told by the people whose lives she touched. On the eve of the opening of Bristol's aerospace museum, a cast of engineers, flight technicians and frequent fliers tell the supersonic story.

programme.title: The Wicker Man
programme.desc: Cult mystery thriller in which a police sergeant visits a remote Scottish isle to search for a missing girl but fears for her safety when he finds a community steeped in paganism. The community deny the girl's existence and this, coupled with the sergeant's Christian background, fuels his suspicions - and growing unease - as the investigation continues.

programme.title: Why the Industrial Revolution Happened Here
programme.desc: Professor Jeremy Black examines the Industrial Revolution. He explains the unique economic, social and political conditions that by the 19th century, led to Britain becoming the richest, most powerful nation on Earth.

programme.title: Scotland: Rome's Final Frontier
programme.desc: Were the ancient Scottish tribes too much for the Roman Empire? Or was Scotland simply not worth conquering? Archaeologist Dr Fraser Hunter looks back on three centuries of contact and conflict with the Roman invaders. Features the first Tay Bridge, the first depiction of tartan, and forgotten Roman camps that once held thirty-five thousand men.

programme.title: Alex Higgins: The People's Champion
programme.desc: One man transfixed television viewers during snooker's golden age - his name was Alex `Hurricane' Higgins. This poignant documentary charts the life of snooker's first genius, from his early days growing up in Belfast to his climb to the top of the sport as two-time world champion. Contributors include Jimmy White, Ronnie O'Sullivan, Dennis Taylor, Steve Davis, and members of the Higgins family.

programme.title: Gold Run
programme.desc: In 1940, the Germans invaded Norway with clear goals in mind: the king, the government, to control the coast, the iron ore and the Norwegian gold reserves. At the same time, a group of resistance fighters was given a most important and secret mission: save Norway's gold.

programme.title: Timewatch
programme.desc: Escapologist Harry Houdini was one of the icons of the 20th century. Restored archive footage and interviews with historians and illusionists recall his extraordinary impact on audiences and reveal the secrets behind some of his most amazing escapes.

programme.title: Scams & Scandals
programme.desc: BBC News goes undercover to expose legal advisers charging migrants thousands of pounds to fabricate immigration claims.
